activity_c.text: Good morning, Nimal.
Today I want to talk about how you are handling repairs and maintenance in the bakery section.
How are things going?
Good morning, madam. Things are going well, but I think some of our processes can be faster.
For example, the dough mixer repair took longer than expected.
Why did it take longer?
Yesterday the motor was weaker than usual, and I had to open the top cover twice.
The wiring was also more complex than I thought.
I wasn’t expecting that.
I see.
When you check the mixer today, what are you going to do first?
I’m going to inspect the belt and test the speed controller.
I must also record everything in the maintenance log because the administration team needs clear reports.
Good.
You have to be systematic.
What about the commercial oven?
Can you handle the temperature sensor adjustment?
Yes, I can, but the new sensor is more sensitive than the old one, so I have to be careful.
The old sensor was slower, but it was easier than this new digital one.
Are you cleaning the proofing cabinet regularly?
Yes, I am.
I clean it every evening, but yesterday I wasn’t able to finish the sanitizing step.
I was too busy with the packaging machine repair.
You must not skip sanitizing.
It is more important than small adjustments.
What happened with the packaging machine?
The sealing arm was hotter than normal, so I checked the thermostat.
It was dirty.
I cleaned it and reset it.
Now it is working properly.
Good.
What are you doing about stock control?
I am updating the ingredient register every day.
The new system is more accurate than the old notebook method, but it is also slower when the Wi-Fi drops.
That happens.
Do you think we need a backup system?
Yes, we can keep printed checklists.
They are simpler than digital forms during busy hours.
That sounds practical.
Keep improving your methods.
It will make the whole production line more efficient than last month.
